title: One-arm Pull-ups - A
texts: Assisted one-arm pull-ups and one-arm lock-offs

This workout is designed to help you work towards completing a one-arm pull-up and towards assisting in the development of maximum pulling strength.

Part 1 of the workout contains assisted one-arm pull-ups. Use enough assistance to allow you to complete the required workout sets and reps in good form. During the last reps of this part of the workout, you should be close to failure due to the high intensity. This will mean you are developing maximal strength. If you cannot complete the listed volume in full without failing, increase the assistance in your next session. 

You can start the pull-up with a slight bend in your elbow if this is more comfortable. Switch arms between sets to create a rest period of 3-4 minutes between the same arm being used.

You can either use a resistance band or counterweight pulley set up to create the correct assistance. Please note how much assistance was used to track progress.

Rest at least 5 minutes before part 2.

Part 2 of the workout involves one arm lock offs. You should be able to complete this at body weight or with minimal assistance to complete this workout effectively. Complete a 5-second lock-off on one arm. Immediately switch to the alternate arm for the following 5 seconds. Complete this twice on each arm to complete one set. There are 3 sets in total. Each lock-off should be held at 90 degrees elbow flexion.
